usage: archive-session.py [-h] --role {clean,spec} [--out OUT]
                          [--archived-by ARCHIVED_BY]
                          transcript

Archives a finished session's transcript into sessions/ (R-CLEAN-3).

  archive-session.py TRANSCRIPT.jsonl --role clean|spec [--out sessions/<role>]

Run it at the start of the next session (never on the live session). A
clean session archives only clean sessions; a spec session may archive
either (sessions/README.md). It copies the transcript to
`sessions/<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` (the date is
the UTC date of its first entry), along with any subagent transcripts
(`<id>/subagents/*.jsonl` next to it) into `<same name>.subagents/`. It
redacts:
  - tokens and keys (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, bearer tokens, private keys);
  - e-mail addresses, except no-reply addresses;
  - account and organisation IDs;
  - private paths: home folders become `~`, and per-user temp folders are
    shortened;
  - the local user names seen in those paths, wherever they appear, and
    `*.local` host names;
  - in clean transcripts only: the lines of a git summary (a merge's
    diffstat, `create mode` and `delete mode` lines) that name files under
    vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/. Each run of such lines
    becomes one note saying how many were removed. A name shortened to
    `.../tail` counts when its tail matches only such files.
It writes `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside the copy, saying what was
redacted and how many times, with the SHA-256 of the original and of the
copy. Every redacted line must still parse as JSON. It refuses to overwrite
an existing archive.

positional arguments:
  transcript

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --role {clean,spec}
  --out OUT             where to put it (default: sessions/<role>/)
  --archived-by ARCHIVED_BY
                        the session doing the archiving, for the note

# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

## Rulesets

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
GitHub API:

| What | ID or fingerprint |
|------|-------------------|
| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |

The deploy key's private half was generated in the session's scratch
folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new

1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):

# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs

as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

# Plan

An original, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket
synthesizer (JieLi AC791N: two pi32v2 cores, 240x240 LCD, key matrix, rotary
encoders, I2S audio), written clean-room so it can ship inside the
F-Emulator iOS app, provably independent of the FM-1's GPL community
firmwares.

Each milestone has its own prompt (`docs/prompts/<Mx>.md`) and its own fresh
session. Roles are defined in CONTRIBUTING.md; requirement IDs are in
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md.

## Milestones

### M0a: foundation (firmware side)
Repo, rules, roles, exposure register, records, signing, toolchain, SDK, CI.
No firmware code yet; a placeholder translation unit proves the pipeline.
- Requirements: R-PROC-1..4, R-REC-1..2, R-REPRO-1..5, R-BUILD-1,
  R-LIC-1..2, R-PUB-1..2, R-CLEAN-1..5.
- Done when: the repo exists with the bootstrap commit and rulesets; CI on a
  pull request runs reuse lint, the commit-message check, the low-profile
  check, the toolchain container build with its checksum and the
  byte-for-byte double build; the owner's signed merge produces the first
  record with a pending OpenTimestamps proof; `tools/reproduce` works;
  EXPOSURE.md and PROVENANCE.md are complete; nothing forbidden was opened.
- Status 2026-10-22: pull request #1 merged as `2fd28219`. Its record
  (`records/2fd28219…/` on `records`) has 13 checks PASS and C-MERGE FAIL
  under the merge rule of the time (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge policy and its
  history"), with a pending OpenTimestamps proof (three calendars).
  `tools/reproduce 2fd28219` on the owner's Mac: REPRODUCED (both outputs
  match the record).

### M0b: harness (spec side)
Vendor the emulator crates `fm1-isa`, `fm1-core`, `fm1-soc` from the public
upstream `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` at a pinned commit, with its MIT licence,
into `vendor/emulator/` (never the rest of that repo). Build the harness: a
Rust library and `fwtest` CLI that boots a raw image, runs N emulated ms with
a timed input script, captures RAM, the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV)
and instructions per audio block, detects halts, compares golden files, and
emits JUnit and JSON.
- Requirements: R-REPRO-*, R-LIC-*, new harness requirements (R-HARN-*).
- Done when: `fwtest` runs in CI from a pinned container, its outputs are
  deterministic, and `tools/clean-setup.sh` excludes `vendor/emulator/` and
  `harness/` from clean clones.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0b, spec side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Setup** (pull request #3): the spec folder, its hand-made settings kept
    and guarded, M0a's transcripts archived in `sessions/clean/`; spec-side
    transcripts go to `sessions/spec/`, which clean folders leave out and
    deny (R-SEP-2).
  - **Emulator** (pull request #4): three crates vendored at upstream commit
    `43ed5580`, reproducible by `tools/fetch-emulator.sh` with a tree hash
    (C-EMU-PIN). One patch, to the workspace manifest only.
  - **Harness** (pull request #4): `fwtest`, a Rust library and CLI with no
    third-party crates, built offline in a container on digest-pinned bases
    (Rust 1.99.0). It boots raw images, takes timed inputs, captures RAM,
    the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV), instructions per audio block
    and the debug console, tells faults, halts and hangs apart, compares
    golden files, and writes JSON and JUnit. Its own tests: 23 cargo tests
    and a 13-case suite on 12 small test images built with the pinned
    toolchain. The suite's outputs were byte-identical in two amd64
    containers at different paths and on Apple Silicon natively.
  - **Separation**: docs/HARNESS.md (the clean side's manual) and
    docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md; checks C-SEP-TERMS, C-CLEAN-FOLDER and
    C-FWTEST-PIN; requirements R-SEP-1..3 and R-HARN-1..10.
  - **Merged**: #3 as `0ad38801`, #4 as `5d4d6fd2`. The records for both
    merges are PASS, with every check run, none skipped. The second
    record's `harness/` holds the suite's JSON, JUnit and output hashes.
  - **Publishing**: `.github/workflows/fwtest-image.yml` pushed the image
    built from `5d4d6fd2` as
    `ghcr.io/japes98/small-beeps@sha256:fa74baf9…` (public; pulls without
    logging in). `config/fwtest-image` pins it, and the suite run through
    `tools/fwtest` with it gives all 47 output files with the same SHA-256
    as that record.
  - **Before the next clean session**, in the clean folder, from a shell:
    `export GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; git fetch origin;` then
    `env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git merge -q --no-stat --ff-only origin/main`
    (only the folder's own files are fetched; without `--no-stat` the merge

    happened in clean maintenance session 1), then `tools/clean-setup.sh`.
    Its live settings predate the new deny rule and the lazy-fetch

each with its source. Facts whose only source is the emulator are marked as
such. It also maps fwtest's key, LED and encoder numbers to the panel and
the key matrix, and covers what docs/HARNESS.md defers to it (the memories,
the second core's release, the audio output's format and rate, the debug
message register), and answers any open spec requests.
- Done when: reviewed for "facts, not code" before the firmware side reads it.
- Requirements: R-SPEC-1..4.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0c, spec side, on the owner's Mac):

    and checks none of their blobs arrive (a control merge with a summary
    fetches 6).
  - **The spec** (pull request #9): `docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, 47 entries
    (HW-1 to HW-47: 38 confirmed, 9 emulator-only) for M0d to M4, flash
    preliminary for M7, and 12 open questions. Sources: the JieLi SDK,
    FM-1-RE's hardware documents, the ST7789V datasheet, the panel's
    printed labels (the owner's app screenshot, `docs/sources/`, and

    subagent given only the spec, CONTRIBUTING.md and the rules;
    its report and the response are in `docs/reviews/M0c-spec-review.md`.

    kept), C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS; C-SEP-TERMS now scans the two doors for
    emulator-only identifiers.
  - **Found on the way**: while an image waits, fwtest's captures can come
    several milliseconds late; docs/HARNESS.md ("Time") now says so.
  - No spec requests were open. M0d (firmware side) is next.

### M0d: smallest firmware (firmware side, next)
Startup, linker script and `main` (a marker word, a heartbeat), written only
from `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the SDK and FM-1-RE's documents; booted and checked
with `fwtest`. Design choices explained in docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md.
- Requirements: R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-2, R-BUILD-1.
- Done when: CI boots the image in the harness and the record shows the
  marker word and heartbeat.

### M0e: audit and performance
- **Similarity audit** (spec side): an isolated CI job fetches the GPL
  firmwares at pinned commits, compares our firmware against them with JPlag
  (SDK as base code, `vendor/` excluded, an unrelated permissive embedded C
  project scored as a control), and publishes scores and file names only.
- **Performance tracking** (firmware side): per-commit size and RAM, later
  emulated instructions per audio block. A 3% regression gate on
  instructions per audio block; per-milestone budgets for size and RAM,
  raised only by a pull request that says why.
- Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-PERF-1, R-PERF-2.

### M1 to M9 (firmware side)
- **M1** boot: clocks, interrupts, timer.
- **M2** screen.
- **M3** keys, encoders, pot, LEDs.
- **M4** audio.
- **M5** the FM engine.
- **M6** MIDI in.
- **M7** flash storage.
- **M8** UI and original presets (no Yamaha factory voices).
- **M9** packaging, and a raw-image boot path in the app.

### Level 2: real hardware
- **M10** recovery kit.
- **M11** USB-MIDI and the update handler.
- **M12** hardware checklist.

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer: not yet investigated.*
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with

synthesizer (JieLi AC791N: two pi32v2 cores, 240x240 LCD, key matrix, rotary

firmwares.

session. Roles are defined in CONTRIBUTING.md; requirement IDs are in
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md.

- Done when: CI boots the image in the harness and the record shows the

| R-SEP-1 | Spec-side text discipline: what the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` only through `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` and `docs/HARNESS.md`. Spec-side commit messages, pull request texts and files elsewhere (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) carry no emulator internals (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Spec-side text discipline"). C-SEP-TERMS finds identifiers that occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in the files, commit messages and pull request texts the firmware side reads; people review `docs/HARNESS.md` and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. | M0b | C-SEP-TERMS; review |
| R-SEP-2 | Spec-side session transcripts are archived only in `sessions/spec/`, which clean folders leave out and their settings deny reading; clean sessions never open it, and the transcript check still works without it. A fresh clean folder has none of `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` or `sessions/spec/` on disk or in its `.git`, denies reading all three, and keeps them out even when the firmware side's tools and history commands run in it or it is updated (clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off). | M0b | C-UNIT, C-DENY-LISTS, C-TRANSCRIPTS, C-CLEAN-FOLDER |
| R-SEP-3 | `tools/fwtest` runs only the fwtest image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image` (no tags), and records which image it ran; the record notes the pinned image. | M0b | C-FWTEST-PIN |
| R-HARN-1 | `fwtest` boots a raw image as docs/HARNESS.md says (load address, size limit, entry, initial state, memory), and refuses images it can't load. | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-2 | A timed input script drives keys, encoders, the pot and MIDI in, in the text format docs/HARNESS.md gives. | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-3 | Captures, as asked: RAM regions, the LCD as PNG, LED duty, the flash chip, audio as WAV, instructions per audio block, the debug console. | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-4 | A fault, a halt and a hang (watchdog) are detected and told apart by exit code; bad input has its own code. | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-5 | Golden files compare exactly, unless a tolerance file allows a documented difference (PNG pixels, WAV samples, CSV numbers). | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-6 | Determinism: the same image, script and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs on every run and machine (no JIT, no host time, no environment influence). | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-B, C-HARNESS-DET |
| R-HARN-7 | Every run writes `result.json` and `junit.xml`; the harness suite's are kept in the commit's record (`harness/`). | M0b | C-HARNESS-TEST, C-HARNESS-SUITE-A |
| R-HARN-8 | fwtest builds in a container whose bases are pinned by digest, offline, with the Rust toolchain pinned and no third-party crates (Cargo.lock lists path crates only); the harness's test images rebuild identically with the pinned toolchain. | M0b | C-HARNESS-IMAGE, C-HARNESS-IMAGES |
| R-HARN-9 | The harness runs raw images only: it never uses the vendored crates' update-package or stock-boot paths, nor anything of M-VAVE's. | M0b | C-HARNESS-SCOPE |
| R-HARN-10 | The firmware side's wrapper `tools/fwtest` runs the published image with no network, as linux/amd64, with the working folder read-only and only `--out` writable. | M0b | C-FWTEST-PIN |
| R-SPEC-1 | Every entry in `docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md` has an ID (`HW-n`, never reused, renumbered or removed: a corrected fact gets a new ID and the old entry is marked superseded), the fact, its sources, its standing (`confirmed`, `emulator-only`, or `superseded by HW-n`) and the milestone that needs it. A confirmed entry cites a source other than the emulator model; every experiment it cites exists. | M0c | C-SPEC-LINT, C-UNIT |

| R-SPEC-3 | `docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md` holds facts, never code, pseudo-code or procedures copied from code, and nothing derived from forbidden material. # Toolchain and SDK

## JieLi Linux toolchain (PROVENANCE P-1)

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Name | `jieli-linux-toolchains-20250324.1` |
| Published at | `https://pkgman.jieliapp.com/s/linux-toolchain` (vendor short link) |
| Pinned URL | `https://jl-update.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/jieli-linux-toolchains-20250324.1.tar.xz` |
| Size | 26,009,040 bytes |
| SHA-256 | `f686586bcfb45e0f0bb27fd2b39c7a7f313cb4f0e88a66a14da621ffa8225958` |
| MD5 (server ETag) | `22a619513462abfc4d86ed50b2922ef7` |
| Server Last-Modified | Mon, 24 Mar 2025 02:39:21 GMT |
| Downloaded | 2026-10-21 |
| Contents | Clang/LLVM 4.0.1 with a pi32v2 backend; GNU Binutils ld 2.26.51.20160621 (targets `elf32-pi32v2`); Linux x86-64 binaries |

**The short link has moved on.** On 2026-10-21 the short link redirected to
`jieli-linux-toolchains-20260730.1.tar.xz` (a newer release), not the pinned
20250324.1. The pinned file is still served at its direct URL, which is what
`tools/Dockerfile` uses. Moving to a newer toolchain is a deliberate change
in its own pull request, with a new SHA-256 here.

### How it is used

- `tools/Dockerfile` downloads the pinned URL, checks the SHA-256 above
  (`sha256sum -c`; the build fails on any mismatch), and unpacks only
  `common/` and `pi32v2/` into `/opt/jieli` in a locally built image.
- The archive and the image are **never committed or published**: not in this
  repository, not in releases, and not pushed to any registry. CI builds the
  image fresh every run. `.gitignore` excludes `*.tar.xz`, and check
  C-NO-TOOLCHAIN fails if any tracked file looks like part of the toolchain.
- We compile with `clang -target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib`
  and link with the toolchain's `ld`. We never link the toolchain's C library
  or its other runtime libraries (R-BUILD-1).

### Licence and terms files found inside

The archive has 695 entries. A search of every path for licence, copying,
notice, terms, EULA, readme and copyright found one file:

- `README.md` (Chinese, about 20 lines): usage notes only. After unpacking
  there are `common/`, `pi32/`, `pi32v2/` and `q32s/` directories; each chip
  family's tools are in its own directory, so set `CC` and similar variables
  in the Makefile; raise the open-file limit (`ulimit -n 8192`) before
  linking, or `ld` may fail with "File format not recognized". **No licence,
  copyright or terms of use.**

No other licence or terms file is present. The toolchain's licence terms are
therefore **unknown**, which is why we never redistribute it. It contains
components normally released under open licences (LLVM/Clang, GNU Binutils,
a newlib C library: `include/newlib.h` and libraries), but the archive
carries none of their licence texts.

### Compiler builtins

Clang's builtins (helpers such as 64-bit division the compiler may call)
would come from `pi32v2/lib/<variant>/libcompiler-rt.a` in the archive. That
is JieLi's build of LLVM's compiler-rt. Upstream compiler-rt of the LLVM 4.x
era is dual-licensed under the University of Illinois/NCSA licence and the
MIT licence. JieLi's build ships no licence text and no source, so we cannot
confirm what is in it. **We don't link it.** `-nostdlib` keeps it out, and
when the firmware needs builtins, our own runtime will provide them (M0d and
later). If that ever changes, the change records the reason here.

### Risk

If the download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy of exactly this
archive, matched by the SHA-256 above. Every released binary stays
verifiable without the toolchain, because each record lists its output
hashes. To preserve the archive, a copy is kept in a separate **private**
repository, `japes98/small-beeps-toolchain`, as a release asset, only for
preservation. It is never public and never linked from releases.
*Status: see the end of this file.*

## JieLi AC79 SDK (PROVENANCE P-2)

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Repository | `https://gitee.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` |
| Branch | `release/AC79NN_SDK_V1.2.0` (the repository's HEAD) |
| Pinned commit | `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, "AC79NN_SDK_V1.2.14_2026-10-13" |
| Licence | Apache License 2.0 (top-level `LICENSE`) |
| Fetched by | `tools/fetch-sdk.sh` (checks each file against `vendor/jieli-sdk/SHA256SUMS`) |

### What we take

Only these files, unmodified, under `vendor/jieli-sdk/` (the AC791N is the
SDK's `wl82` CPU family):

- `LICENSE`: the SDK's Apache-2.0 licence;
- `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/WL82.h`: special-function register
  definitions;
- `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/csfr.h`: core register definitions, which
  `WL82.h` includes.

More headers are added only when a firmware milestone needs them, each in
its own commit, logged in PROVENANCE.md.

### Licence coverage

The SDK's top-level `LICENSE` is the Apache License 2.0 and covers the
repository. Many SDK headers also carry JieLi's own notice in the form
"Copyright:(c)JIELI 2011 @ , All Rights Reserved." This is a copyright
notice; it doesn't grant other terms, and the repository-level Apache-2.0
grant applies. `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` carry no per-file notice. `REUSE.toml`
marks `vendor/jieli-sdk/**` as Apache-2.0, copyright JIELI.

### Not used: parts with other or unknown terms

These parts of the SDK are **not used** and never vendored:

- **Prebuilt libraries:** 151 `.a` archives under `cpu/wl82/`, plus 3 under
  `include_lib/c++/` and 3 under `include_lib/newlib/` (binary only; terms
  unknown beyond the repository licence; we use none).
- **Windows tool binaries:** `.exe`/`.dll` files under `tools/utils/` and
  `cpu/wl82/tools/`. Not inspected; judging by their names (`make.exe`,
  `libiconv2.dll`, `libintl3.dll`), some are likely GNU tools under their own
  licences.
- **Bundled third-party code under its own licences**, including
  `apps/common/example/third_party/` (coremark, FlashDB, littlefs, ugfx's
  tinygl), `include_lib/net/uC-HTTPc/` (own LICENSE and NOTICE),
  `include_lib/system/os/POSIX/` (own LICENSE) and `lib/net/mbedtls_3_4_0/`
  (own LICENSE).
- **Linker scripts** under `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/` (`*.ld`): not used.
  M0d writes its own linker script from `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

## Preservation copy status

- 2026-10-22 (UTC): uploaded with the owner's approval by session M0a.
  Private repository `japes98/small-beeps-toolchain`, release
  `toolchain-20250324.1`, asset `jieli-linux-toolchains-20250324.1.tar.xz`.
  Downloaded back and checked: SHA-256
  `f686586bcfb45e0f0bb27fd2b39c7a7f313cb4f0e88a66a14da621ffa8225958`
  (matches). The release notes repeat the hash and say the terms are unknown
  and that it is not for redistribution.

# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- When core 0 waits (the wait-for-interrupt instruction, or a tight loop
  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.
- While core 0 waits, a capture can come late. Each wait can move time
  ahead to the next timed event, and fwtest looks only between runs of up
  to 1024 instructions, so a capture (an LED sample, the watchdog, the end
  of the run) can be taken several milliseconds after the time asked when
  the image waits often, for example between interrupts every 100 µs.
  `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run really ended. To capture
  at an exact time, keep core 0 busy (not waiting) around it.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- When core 0 waits (the wait-for-interrupt instruction, or a tight loop
  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.
- While core 0 waits, a capture can come late. Each wait can move time
  ahead to the next timed event, and fwtest looks only between runs of up
  to 1024 instructions, so a capture (an LED sample, the watchdog, the end
  of the run) can be taken several milliseconds after the time asked when
  the image waits often, for example between interrupts every 100 µs.
  `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run really ended. To capture
  at an exact time, keep core 0 busy (not waiting) around it.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources

| Key | Source |
|-----|--------|
| SDK | JieLi AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), commit `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, Apache-2.0 (PROVENANCE P-2, P-10). `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` are vendored in `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/`; the other files cited are at the same commit and path prefix. Line numbers refer to that commit. |
| RE | AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL), commit `ec832f281ca165a7d5e0722985f3acb1465046d5`: its hardware and boot documents `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md`, `docs/io/01-boot.md`, `docs/io/03-audio-dac.md`, `docs/io/08-display.md`, `docs/io/09-storage.md` (PROVENANCE P-9). Only their hardware facts are used here. |
| DS | Sitronix ST7789V datasheet, version 1.3 (2014-03), 316 pages, from `https://www.newhavendisplay.com/appnotes/datasheets/LCDs/ST7789V.pdf`, SHA-256 `8ecf0e43…5d04ca1` (PROVENANCE P-11). Page numbers as printed. |
| PANEL | The FM-1's printed panel labels, from two sources that agree: the owner's screenshot of the F-Emulator app's panel with its default labels, `docs/sources/panel-app-default-labels.png` (secondary: the app's drawing of the panel); and M-VAVE's product photo of the FM-1, `https://www.m-vave.com/images/products/fm-1.webp` on `https://www.m-vave.com/product.html?id=fm-1`, accessed 2026-10-22, SHA-256 `e610a746…df14b95`, not copied into this repository (PROVENANCE P-12). Only the printed labels are taken from them. The owner chose these two sources. |
| HARNESS | docs/HARNESS.md, fwtest's manual. It is the spec side's own description of fwtest, so it never confirms an entry on its own. |
| E-n | A spec-side black-box experiment: a small image run in fwtest (the pinned image, `config/fwtest-image`). Its result is stated in the entry. C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS re-runs every one in CI, so a cited result that stops holding fails CI. |

---

## 1. The raw image and boot (M0d)

### HW-1: Load address and entry
- Fact: In fwtest, the image is a flat binary whose first byte is at
  `0x02000000`, the start of the code window, and core 0 starts executing
  at that first byte. Link the image to run there.
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); E-1: an image whose first
  instructions record the registers ran from its first byte.
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

### HW-2: Registers at entry
- Fact: In fwtest, at the first instruction r0 = `0x01C7FC00` and every
  other register reads 0, including `sp`, `usp`, `ssp`, `icfg` and `psr`.
  No stack is usable until the image sets one. `cnum` reads 0 (core 0).
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); E-1: r0 = `0x01C7FC00`; r2 to r15,
  `sp`, `usp`, `ssp`, `icfg`, `psr` and `cnum` read 0. r1 could not be
  observed (the experiment needed it first): for r1 the only source is
  HARNESS.
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

### HW-3: Core 0 starts in user mode
- Fact: In fwtest, core 0 starts in user mode. An interrupt taken in user
  mode continues on the supervisor stack pointer `ssp` (the user `sp` is
  kept in `usp`), and its return goes back to user mode and `usp`. An
  interrupt taken in supervisor mode stays on the current stack. So `ssp`
  must point at a valid stack before interrupts are enabled.
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); the emulator model.
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M0d, M1

### HW-4: The block r0 points to at entry
- Fact: In fwtest, r0 points to a 64-byte block in RAM whose first word
  holds `0x01C7FC40` (the address just past the block) and whose other
  bytes are 0. On the chip, the loader that starts an installed app passes
  a boot-parameter block in r0; its contents are not described here (see
  Q-11).

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## 3. Interrupts (M1)

### HW-18: The vector table
- Fact: The handler for interrupt source n is the 32-bit address in the
  word at `0x01C7FE00 + 4 × n`, in RAM. The firmware writes the table. The
  slot of source 126 (`0x01C7FFF8`) is also core 1's start address (HW-9);
  the slot of source 127 (`0x01C7FFFC`) has no other use known here. In
  fwtest both cores use this one table.
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 114-123 (`ISR_ENTRY 0x1c7fe00`, sources up
  to 127); RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §1 and §4.1; E-3, E-9: handlers
  installed this way ran.

- Needed by: M1

### HW-19: Interrupt source numbers

  11 the audio link `JL_ALNK0` (the SDK's `IRQ_ALNK_IDX`), 16 SPI1 (LCD),

  source 62 on the chip; it never fires in fwtest, HW-14.) The SDK's
  `hwi.h` lists the rest.

- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-20: Enabling a source, and its priority
- Fact: Each core has its own enable and priority words, `ICFG00` to
  `ICFG31`: core 0's at `0x01EEF100` to `0x01EEF17C`, core 1's at
  `0x01EEF300` to `0x01EEF37C`. Source n uses 4 bits of word n / 8, at bit
  position 4 × (n mod 8): bit 0 enables it, bits 1-3 are its priority 0-7.
  A higher number is a higher priority. A source interrupts only the cores
  whose words enable it.

  ("0~7, larger is higher"); RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §4.1 (the 4-bit
  encoding and the two arrays); E-3, E-9 (sources enabled this way).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, RE, E-3)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-21: The global interrupt gates
- Fact: A core takes interrupts only while both gates are open: bit 8 of
  its special register `icfg` (the master enable; not to be confused with
  the `ICFG00`-`ICFG31` words of HW-20) and the enable set by the

  is clear: set it and execute `sti` before expecting interrupts.

  the handler returns with `rti`. A handler compiled with the toolchain's
  interrupt function attribute returns correctly. A running handler can be
  interrupted by a pending source of higher priority only after it has
  stored `reti` to its stack, and only until it loads `reti` back; sources
  of the same or lower priority wait until it returns. When several enabled
  sources are pending, the one with the highest priority is taken; between

- Needed by: M1

  time skips ahead to the next timed event, and with interrupts enabled the

  same way. Waiting therefore costs almost no instructions, and captures may
  come late while core 0 waits (HARNESS, "Time"). What `idle` does on the
  chip with interrupts masked is part of Q-10.

  interrupt).
- Standing: confirmed (E-3)
- Needed by: M1
