## 5. The LCD (M2)
## Open questions

What isn't known, or is known only from material the spec may not use. A
spec request can turn one into a fact.

- **Q-1. Other RAM on the chip.** Whether the chip has RAM at `0x01F00000`
  and `0x04000000` (HW-7), how much, and whether it can be used. The SDK's
  layout names a cache RAM at `0x01F20000` and an external SDRAM window at
  `0x04000000`.
- **Q-2. Clock set-up on the chip.** Which registers and steps set the PLL
  and system clock on real hardware, and which rates the chip supports
  (fwtest needs none). Settled by a spec request answered from permitted
  sources, or by an experiment on hardware.
- **Q-3. TIMER0-3 prescaler settings other than 0 and 2.** Measure with a
  black-box test, or ask.
- **Q-4. The core tick timer's period on the chip.** Which clock `TTMR_PRD`
  counts on real hardware (fwtest always uses 10 ms).
- **Q-5. A debug console on the chip.** Whether `DBG_MSG` writes go
  anywhere on real hardware (the SDK marks it read-only), or which UART
  pins could carry debug output.
- **Q-6. LCD wiring.** Which pins carry SPI1's clock, data and chip select
  (and the `JL_IOMAP` selection for them), whether the panel has a reset
  pin and a backlight pin, and which ones; the panel's orientation and its
  offset within the controller's 240 × 320 memory. fwtest needs none of
  them.
- **Q-7. The panel's wiring on the chip.** Whether the board's key matrix,
  encoders and LEDs are wired as fwtest presents them (HW-33, HW-34,
  HW-38, HW-42: the pins, the shift registers, an LED for every key, which
  physical turn is "clockwise"); pull-ups, directions and drive for the
  pins, LED polarity and current. fwtest needs no pin set-up.
- **Q-8. The other ADC channels.** What channel 3 and the other channels
  carry on the board (fwtest gives them fixed values).
- **Q-9. Audio on the chip.** How `JL_ALNK0`'s output reaches the DAC or
  codec on real hardware, which bits of each word it uses, its clock set-up
  and true rate, and the analog set-up (FM-1-RE's audio document names DAC
  registers at `0x00012F00`; not used here).
- **Q-10. Interrupt details on the chip.** Whether the chip switches
  stacks on an interrupt from user mode exactly as HW-3 says; its nesting
  rules and choice among pending sources (HW-22); whether the two cores
  share one vector table; what `idle` does with interrupts masked (HW-24).
  The toolchain's interrupt attribute works in fwtest.
- **Q-11. Booting on the chip.** The contents of the boot-parameter block
  the loader passes in r0, and whether a raw image can be started on real
  hardware without M-VAVE's loader (PLAN.md, M9 risk), and whether such an
  image can release core 1 as HW-9 says.
- **Q-12. MIDI input.** UART1 and the MIDI jack are not covered here (M6
  will ask).

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -Os -g
            -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=."
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    clang $CFLAGS -c firmware/src/placeholder.c -o "$out/placeholder.o"
    ld -nostdlib -e placeholder -o "$out/placeholder.elf" "$out/placeholder.o"
    set +x
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in "$out"/placeholder.o "$out"/placeholder.elf; do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

{

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Runs every check and writes the test record (R-PROC-4, R-REC-1).

  record.py run --out DIR [--only C-A,C-B] [--skip C-X] [--with-merge]
      Runs the checks in CHECKS, writes DIR/report.json, DIR/report.md,
      DIR/logs/<check>.log, DIR/outputs/ (the build outputs) and
      DIR/SHA256SUMS (of all of those). Exit status 1 if any check failed.
  record.py compare --record REPORT.json --outputs DIR
      Compares DIR/SHA256SUMS with the outputs listed in a record
      (used by tools/reproduce). Exit status 1 on any difference.

Environment: COMMIT_RANGE (for C-COMMIT-MSG, default: every commit reachable
from HEAD), GITHUB_* (recorded, and used by C-LOW-PROFILE and C-MERGE).
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
PY = sys.executable or "python3"
SCHEMA = 1


def _low_profile_cmd():
    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true":
        return [PY, "-I", "tools/check-low-profile.py", "--require-api"]
    return [PY, "-I", "tools/check-low-profile.py", "--offline"]


def _commit_range():
    return os.environ.get("COMMIT_RANGE") or "..HEAD"


# Each check: id, title, requirement IDs, and either a command (list, or a
# function returning one, run from the repository root) or an internal
# function name. "records_only" checks run only with --with-merge.
CHECKS = [
    {"id": "C-UNIT", "title": "Unit tests of the tools",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1", "R-PROC-4", "R-REC-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-4", "R-PUB-1",
              "R-SEP-2", "R-SPEC-1", "R-SPEC-3"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-t", ".", "-v"]},
    {"id": "C-REUSE", "title": "reuse lint (SPDX licence and copyright on every file)",
     "reqs": ["R-LIC-1", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["reuse", "lint"]},
    {"id": "C-COMMIT-MSG", "title": "Commit messages follow .gitmessage",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1"],
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/check-commit-msg.py", "--range", _commit_range()]},
    {"id": "C-LOW-PROFILE", "title": "Low profile: name, description, topics, README",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-1"], "cmd": _low_profile_cmd},
    {"id": "C-SECRETS", "title": "No secrets in tracked files",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "secrets"]},
    {"id": "C-NO-TOOLCHAIN", "title": "No toolchain parts or binaries tracked",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-1"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "no-toolchain"]},
    {"id": "C-DENY-LISTS", "title": "Claude Code deny lists never drop an entry",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-4", "R-SEP-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-deny-lists.py"]},
    {"id": "C-TRANSCRIPTS", "title": "Archived session transcripts: banners and forbidden material",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-5", "R-SEP-2"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-transcripts.py"]},
    {"id": "C-SEP-TERMS", "title": "No emulator-only identifiers outside the spec side's folders",
     "reqs": ["R-SEP-1", "R-SPEC-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-emulator-terms.py"]},
    {"id": "C-SPEC-LINT", "title": "docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md: every entry has an ID, fact, sources, standing; no code; IDs kept",
     "reqs": ["R-SPEC-1", "R-SPEC-3"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-hardware-spec.py"]},
    {"id": "C-CLEAN-FOLDER", "title": "A fresh clean folder has no spec-side files and denies them",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-1", "R-SEP-2"], "needs": "vendor/emulator", "cmd": ["sh", "tools/check-clean-folder.sh"]},
    {"id": "C-FWTEST-PIN", "title": "tools/fwtest runs an image pinned by digest",
     "reqs": ["R-SEP-3", "R-HARN-10"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-fwtest-pin.py"]},
    {"id": "C-SDK-PIN", "title": "Vendored SDK files match the pinned commit",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-5", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["sh", "tools/fetch-sdk.sh", "--verify"]},
    {"id": "C-EMU-PIN", "title": "Vendored emulator crates match the pinned upstream commit",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-6", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["sh", "tools/fetch-emulator.sh", "--verify"]},
    {"id": "C-IMAGE", "title": "Build container (pinned base, toolchain SHA-256 checked)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-1", "R-REPRO-2"], "cmd": ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "image"]},
    {"id": "C-BUILD-A", "title": "Build A in a fresh container (source at /mnt/small-beeps-src)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3", "R-BUILD-1"],
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", os.path.join(OUT, "build-a")]},
    {"id": "C-BUILD-B", "title": "Build B in a fresh container (source at another path)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3"],
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", os.path.join(OUT, "build-b"),
                     "--src-mount", "/tmp/elsewhere/small-beeps-src-b"]},
    {"id": "C-DETERMINISM", "title": "Builds A and B are byte-identical",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3"], "internal": "determinism"},
    # The harness (spec side): skipped where harness/ isn't on disk.
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-SCOPE", "title": "The harness uses no update-package or stock-boot paths",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-9"], "needs": "harness", "cmd": ["sh", "harness/ci.sh", "scope"]},
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-IMAGES", "title": "Harness test images rebuild identically with the pinned toolchain",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-8"], "needs": "harness", "cmd": ["sh", "harness/tests/images/build.sh", "--check"]},
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-IMAGE", "title": "fwtest container (pinned bases, offline build)",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-8"], "needs": "harness", "cmd": ["sh", "harness/ci.sh", "image"]},
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-TEST", "title": "The harness's own tests (cargo test in the container)",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-1", "R-HARN-2", "R-HARN-3", "R-HARN-4", "R-HARN-5", "R-HARN-6", "R-HARN-7"],
     "needs": "harness", "cmd": ["sh", "harness/ci.sh", "test"]},
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-SUITE-A", "title": "Harness suite, run A (fresh container, tests at /mnt/harness-a)",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-1", "R-HARN-2", "R-HARN-3", "R-HARN-4", "R-HARN-5", "R-HARN-7"], "needs": "harness",
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "harness/ci.sh", "suite", os.path.join(OUT, "harness-a"), "/mnt/harness-a"]},
    {"id": "C-HARNESS-SUITE-B", "title": "Harness suite, run B (fresh container, tests at another path)",
     "reqs": ["R-HARN-6"], "needs": "harness",
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "harness/ci.sh", "suite", os.path.join(OUT, "harness-b"), "/tmp/elsewhere/harness-b"]},

         "- Subject: %s" % report["subject"],
         "- Tree: `%s`" % report["tree"],
         "- Written: %s" % report["created_utc"],
         "- Overall: **%s**" % report["overall"]]

    if gh.get("GITHUB_RUN_ID"):
        L.append("- CI run: https://github.com/%s/actions/runs/%s"

    for c in report["checks"]:

    for name, digest in sorted(report["outputs"].items()):

    L += ["", "## Traceability", "", "| Requirement | Checks | Result |",
          "|-------------|--------|--------|"]
    for t in report["traceability"]:
        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (t["requirement"], ", ".join(t["checks"]) or "-",
                                       t["result"]))
    L += ["", "## Environment", "", "```json",
          json.dumps(report["environment"], indent=2, sort_keys=True), "```", ""]
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

def cmd_run(a):
    global OUT
    OUT = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(OUT, "logs"), exist_ok=True)
    only = set(a.only.split(",")) if a.only else None
    skip = set(a.skip.split(",")) if a.skip else set()
    results = []
    for c in CHECKS:
        if only is not None and c["id"] not in only:

        if c["id"] in skip or (c.get("records_only") and not a.with_merge):

        if c.get("needs") and not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(ROOT, c["needs"])):

        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "logs", c["id"] + ".log"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("$ %s\n%s\nexit status %d\n" % (" ".join(argv), log, code))
        print("%-14s %-4s %6.1fs  %s" % (c["id"], result, secs, c["title"]), flush=True)
        results.append({"id": c["id"], "title": c["title"], "reqs": c["reqs"],

            if rel != "SHA256SUMS" and not rel.endswith(".ots"):

# argument must be inside it (relative, or absolute under it). The --out
# folder is created on the host and mounted read-write on its own. The
# container runs as linux/amd64 with no network, as your user. After a run,
# DIR/runner.txt names the image used, for the record.
#
# FWTEST_IMAGE overrides the pinned image (spec side, to try a local build);
# runner.txt then says the image was not the pinned one.
set -eu

PIN_FILE="$ROOT/config/fwtest-image"
pinned=$(grep -v '^#' "$PIN_FILE" | grep . | head -1)

if [ -n "${FWTEST_IMAGE:-}" ]; then
    ref=$FWTEST_IMAGE
    note="not the pinned image (FWTEST_IMAGE); pinned: $pinned"
else
    case "$pinned" in
        *@sha256:????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????) ;;
        *) echo "tools/fwtest: no published image is pinned yet (config/fwtest-image: $pinned)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    ref=$pinned
    note="pinned (config/fwtest-image)"
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = "--image" ]; then
    echo "$ref"
    exit 0
fi

cwd=$(pwd -P)
inside() {
    # a path argument as the container sees it, or an error if it is outside cwd
    case "$1" in
        /*) p=$1 ;;
        *) p="$cwd/$1" ;;
    esac
    d=$(dirname "$p")
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then p="$(cd "$d" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$p")"; fi
    case "$p" in
        "$cwd") echo /work ;;
        "$cwd"/*) echo "/work/${p#"$cwd"/}" ;;
        *) echo "tools/fwtest: $1 is outside the current directory" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
}

quote() { printf "'%s'" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")"; }
out=""
args=""
cmd=${1:-}
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
args=$(quote "$cmd")
positional=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    a=$1

            p=$(inside "$1") || exit 2
            args="$args $a $(quote "$p")"; shift ;;
        --ms|--ram|--lcd|--leds-every|--watchdog)
            [ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "tools/fwtest: $a needs a value" >&2; exit 2; }

    case "$out" in /*) ;; *) out="$cwd/$out" ;; esac
    if [ -e "$out" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$out" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "tools/fwtest: --out $out is not empty" >&2

    fi
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd -P)
    mounts="$mounts -v $(quote "$out"):/out"

eval "docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none --user $(id -u):$(id -g) $mounts -w /work $(quote "$ref") $args"

if [ -n "$out" ]; then
    printf 'image: %s\nstatus: %s\nexit: %d\n' "$ref" "$note" "$code" > "$out/runner.txt"
fi
exit $code

## 0. Start safely

## 2. The firmware

The smallest firmware that proves our own code boots and runs in fwtest:
- our own startup code and linker script, written from the spec, the SDK headers and first principles;
- `main` that writes a marker, then a heartbeat that fwtest can observe over time;
- freestanding C11 plus whatever assembly startup needs; no toolchain C library, nothing prebuilt from the SDK; our own minimal runtime (only what this needs);
- built by tools/build.sh in the pinned toolchain container, deterministic (the CI double build must stay byte-identical);
- every file with SPDX headers; small commits, each with the What/Why/How/Result/Sources/Exposure template.

Write docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md entries for each real choice (memory layout, stack, startup order, how the heartbeat is timed), each citing the HW IDs, SDK files or experiments it rests on. Choose your own designs; where the spec gives requirements, meet them in your own way.

## 3. Tests

- Black-box tests for any emulator-only facts you rely on.
- Each test names the requirements it checks (add R-BOOT-* and any others to docs/REQUIREMENTS.md), and the record's traceability table shows them.

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"

cmd_build() {

    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

# The image's size in bytes, from the symbols firmware/app.ld defines:
# code (code and constants, in the image), data (initialised data: in the
# image and copied to RAM), bss (zeroed RAM, the beacon included), image
# (the raw image's length) and stack (reserved at the top of RAM).
write_size() {
    sym() { nm "$1" | awk -v s="$2" '$3 == s { print $1 }'; }
    hex() { printf '%d' "0x$1"; }
    origin=$(hex 02000000)
    data_load=$(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_load)")
    data=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_start)") ))
    bss=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_start)") ))
    stack=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    printf 'code %d\ndata %d\nbss %d\nimage %d\nstack %d\n' \
        $((data_load - origin)) "$data" "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) "$stack"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    mkdir -p "$out/obj"
    objs=""
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$out/obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    objcopy -O binary -j .text -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$out/app.bin"
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=$(mktemp -d)
    objs=""
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"

# Spec requests

How the firmware side (clean) asks the spec side (exposed) for a hardware
fact it needs, and how the answer comes back, without anything else passing
between them (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles").

## Asking (firmware side)

Add a request at the end of "Requests" below, by pull request:

- a number (`SR-1`, `SR-2`, ...; never reused);
- the date asked;
- the question: one fact about the hardware (an address, a bit, a pin, a
  timing, a protocol step, a limit), asked as narrowly as you can;
- why it is needed: what the firmware is trying to do, the milestone, and
  what you already tried or read (HARDWARE-SPEC.md sections, the JieLi SDK,
  FM-1-RE's documents, datasheets, your own black-box runs in fwtest);
- the status `open`.

Don't ask how another firmware does something, and don't paste or describe
any material you aren't allowed to read. A question about fwtest's
behaviour (a capture, an exit code, an option) is not a spec request: open
an issue or a pull request against docs/HARNESS.md.

## Answering (spec side)

- Answer by adding the fact to `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, with its source, as
  every fact there has (M0c's rules: facts only, never code or code
  structure; a fact whose only source is the emulator is marked so).
- Then set the request's status to `answered`, with a link to the section,
  in the same pull request. Nothing else goes in the request: no code, no
  explanation of how any other firmware or the emulator does it, no
  excerpts.
- If the fact isn't known, say so (`unknown`), with what would settle it
  (a probe on real hardware, a datasheet). If answering would take
  something the spec side may not pass on, say `declined` and why, in
  general terms.
- The spec side's text discipline applies to the whole exchange
  (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Spec-side text discipline"; C-SEP-TERMS checks it).

## Template

```markdown
### SR-<n>: <the question, in a few words>
- Asked: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <who or which session>
- Question: <one fact, asked narrowly>
- Why: <what the firmware needs it for; what was tried or read>
- Status: open | answered (HARDWARE-SPEC.md, "<section>") | unknown | declined
- Answered: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <who or which session>
```

## Requests

None yet.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Runs the firmware's fwtest suite and checks its heartbeat (check
C-FW-SUITE; R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5).

  fw-suite.py --build DIR --out DIR

Copies DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output) to out/fw/app.bin, where
tests/fw/boot.suite expects it, runs the suite through tools/fwtest (the
pinned image), and then checks every case's result.json and the heartbeat
case's beacon captures:

- each case completed: no fault, halt or hang; no unmodelled accesses; core
  1 never ran;
- every beacon holds the marker and the period of 24 000 ticks (1 ms of the
  24 MHz time base, HW-13);
- beats == ticks // period: one beat per whole period of the time base;
- each capture's ticks are no earlier than its time asked, less START_SLACK
  (main starts the time base a few instructions after the image starts),
  and no later than LATE_MS after it (captures can come late while the
  image waits, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
- at the end of the run the time base agrees with fwtest's emulated time
  (result.json's emulated_ms) within START_SLACK: the stated tolerance of
  the heartbeat's timing, 10 microseconds over the run.

Prints what it saw (the marker, and each capture's beats and time) for the
record, and exits 1 if anything failed.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = "tests/fw/boot.suite"
IMAGE = os.path.join("out", "fw", "app.bin")

MARKER = 0x44304253        # "SB0D", firmware/src/sb.h
TICKS_PER_MS = 24000       # HW-13
START_SLACK = 240          # ticks: 10 microseconds
LATE_MS = 5
CAPTURE = re.compile(r"^ram-01c00000-10-(?P<when>[0-9.]+ms|end)\.bin$")


def check_case(name, result):
    """Problems with one case's result.json."""
    run = result.get("run", {})
    problems = []
    if run.get("outcome") != "completed":
        problems.append("%s: outcome %s (%s)" % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("detail")))
    if run.get("unmodelled_accesses"):
        problems.append("%s: unmodelled accesses %s" % (name, run["unmodelled_accesses"]))
    if run.get("instructions", {}).get("core1", 0) != 0:
        problems.append("%s: core 1 ran" % name)
    return problems


def check_beacon(when_ms, data, end_ms=None):
    """Problems with one 16-byte beacon captured at when_ms (the time asked;
    end_ms is result.json's emulated_ms for the capture at the end)."""
    marker, beats, ticks, period = struct.unpack("<4I", data)
    problems = []
    if marker != MARKER:
        problems.append("marker 0x%08x, not 0x%08x" % (marker, MARKER))
    if period != TICKS_PER_MS:
        problems.append("period %d, not %d" % (period, TICKS_PER_MS))
        return problems
    if beats != ticks // period:
        problems.append("%d beats after %d ticks, not %d" % (beats, ticks, ticks // period))
    if end_ms is not None:
        expect = round(end_ms * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not expect - START_SLACK <= ticks <= expect:
            problems.append("%d ticks at the end (%.3f ms), not within %d of %d"
                            % (ticks, end_ms, START_SLACK, expect))
    else:
        low = round(when_ms * TICKS_PER_MS) - START_SLACK
        high = round((when_ms + LATE_MS) * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not low <= ticks <= high:
            problems.append("%d ticks at %s ms, not within %d to %d" % (ticks, when_ms, low, high))
    return problems


def check_heartbeat(case_dir, result):
    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last = [], [], -1
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != 16:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        marker, beats, ticks, _ = struct.unpack("<4I", data)
        lines.append("  %-6s marker 0x%08x  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)"
                     % (when, marker, beats, ticks, ticks / TICKS_PER_MS))
        problems += ["heartbeat %s: %s" % (when, p) for p in
                     check_beacon(when_ms, data, end_ms if when == "end" else None)]
        if beats < last:
            problems.append("heartbeat %s: beats went back from %d to %d" % (when, last, beats))
        last = beats
    return problems, lines


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            print("image size: " + ", ".join(l.strip() for l in f if l.strip()))

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    problems = [] if p.returncode == 0 else ["fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode]

    for name in ("boot", "heartbeat"):
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        if name == "boot":
            for g in sorted(result.get("golden", {}) or {}):
                print("  golden %s: %s" % (g, result["golden"][g]))
        if name == "heartbeat" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(os.path.join(out, name), result)
            problems += more
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

pinned image), and then checks every case's result.json and the heartbeat
case's beacon captures:

- each case completed: no fault, halt or hang; no unmodelled accesses; core
  1 never ran;
- every beacon holds the marker and the period of 24 000 ticks (1 ms of the
  24 MHz time base, HW-13);
- beats == ticks // period: one beat per whole period of the time base;
- each capture's ticks are no earlier than its time asked, less START_SLACK
  (main starts the time base a few instructions after the image starts),
  and no later than LATE_MS after it (captures can come late while the
  image waits, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
- at the end of the run the time base agrees with fwtest's emulated time
  (result.json's emulated_ms) within START_SLACK: the stated tolerance of
  the heartbeat's timing, 10 microseconds over the run.

Prints what it saw (the marker, and each capture's beats and time) for the
record, and exits 1 if anything failed.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = "tests/fw/boot.suite"
IMAGE = os.path.join("out", "fw", "app.bin")

MARKER = 0x44304253        # "SB0D", firmware/src/sb.h
TICKS_PER_MS = 24000       # HW-13
START_SLACK = 240          # ticks: 10 microseconds
LATE_MS = 5
CAPTURE = re.compile(r"^ram-01c00000-10-(?P<when>[0-9.]+ms|end)\.bin$")


def check_case(name, result):
    """Problems with one case's result.json."""
    run = result.get("run", {})
    problems = []
    if run.get("outcome") != "completed":
        problems.append("%s: outcome %s (%s)" % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("detail")))
    if run.get("unmodelled_accesses"):
        problems.append("%s: unmodelled accesses %s" % (name, run["unmodelled_accesses"]))
    if run.get("instructions", {}).get("core1", 0) != 0:
        problems.append("%s: core 1 ran" % name)
    return problems


def check_beacon(when_ms, data, end_ms=None):
    """Problems with one 16-byte beacon captured at when_ms (the time asked;
    end_ms is result.json's emulated_ms for the capture at the end)."""
    marker, beats, ticks, period = struct.unpack("<4I", data)
    problems = []
    if marker != MARKER:
        problems.append("marker 0x%08x, not 0x%08x" % (marker, MARKER))
    if period != TICKS_PER_MS:
        problems.append("period %d, not %d" % (period, TICKS_PER_MS))
        return problems
    if beats != ticks // period:
        problems.append("%d beats after %d ticks, not %d" % (beats, ticks, ticks // period))
    if end_ms is not None:
        expect = round(end_ms * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not expect - START_SLACK <= ticks <= expect:
            problems.append("%d ticks at the end (%.3f ms), not within %d of %d"
                            % (ticks, end_ms, START_SLACK, expect))
    else:
        low = round(when_ms * TICKS_PER_MS) - START_SLACK
        high = round((when_ms + LATE_MS) * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not low <= ticks <= high:
            problems.append("%d ticks at %s ms, not within %d to %d" % (ticks, when_ms, low, high))
    return problems


def check_heartbeat(case_dir, result):
    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last = [], [], -1
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != 16:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        marker, beats, ticks, _ = struct.unpack("<4I", data)
        lines.append("  %-6s marker 0x%08x  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)"
                     % (when, marker, beats, ticks, ticks / TICKS_PER_MS))
        problems += ["heartbeat %s: %s" % (when, p) for p in
                     check_beacon(when_ms, data, end_ms if when == "end" else None)]
        if beats < last:
            problems.append("heartbeat %s: beats went back from %d to %d" % (when, last, beats))
        last = beats
    return problems, lines


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            print("image size: " + ", ".join(l.strip() for l in f if l.strip()))

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    problems = [] if p.returncode == 0 else ["fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode]

    for name in ("boot", "heartbeat"):
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        if name == "boot":
            for g in sorted(result.get("golden", {}) or {}):
                print("  golden %s: %s" % (g, result["golden"][g]))
        if name == "heartbeat" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(os.path.join(out, name), result)
            problems += more
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

cat >> docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md <<'EOF'

### 2026-10-22 M0d: memory layout
- Facts: HW-1 (the image runs from its first byte at `0x02000000`), HW-5
  (the code window shows the flash chip from offset `0x4000`, so at most
  1 MiB less 16 KiB), HW-6 (main RAM is 512 KiB from `0x01C00000` on the
  chip; its top holds the SDK's boot and update area and the vector table),
  HW-4 (the block r0 points to at `0x01C7FC00` in fwtest), HW-7 (fwtest has
  1 MiB of main RAM and two more banks, not known on the chip, Q-1),
  HW-18 (the vector table at `0x01C7FE00`). `firmware/app.ld`.
- Reasoning: code and constants run in place from the image (the window
  is readable and executable), so only data that changes takes RAM. RAM is
  limited to what the chip has and stops at `0x01C7FC00`: that keeps the
  r0 block (wanted later for booting on the chip, Q-11), the SDK's reserved
  area and the vector table out of reach of anything this image does,
  which R-BOOT-5's golden capture checks. Order in RAM: the beacon first,
  at a fixed address the tests name; then zeroed data; then initialised
  data, whose bytes the image carries right after the code; the stack at
  the top. The beacon and `.bss` are one contiguous range, so startup
  clears both with one loop. The linker script asserts the fixed
  addresses and that data never reaches the stack.
- Alternatives: using fwtest's larger RAM (rejected: an image that only
  fits fwtest proves less); putting the beacon in `.data` (rejected: its
  address would move whenever data is added).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the stack
- Facts: HW-2 (every register but r0 is 0 at entry, both stack pointers
  included: no stack until the image sets one), HW-3 (core 0 starts in user
  mode; interrupts would switch to `ssp`, emulator-only), the compiler's
  data layout for pi32v2 (no type is aligned to more than 4 bytes; P-13).
- Reasoning: the first instruction sets `sp` to `0x01C7FC00`, before any C
  runs; 4 KiB is reserved below it. M0d's C uses a few words at most (the
  compiler keeps `sb_start` and `main` in registers), so 4 KiB is ample
  and cheap. The top is 8-byte aligned, more than the data layout needs,
  so nothing changes if 8-byte types arrive. Only the user-mode `sp` is
  set: M0d takes no interrupts, so `ssp` is left for M1, which must set it
  before enabling them (HW-3).
- Alternatives: a stack at the very top of RAM (rejected: it would run
  through the reserved area and the vector table).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: startup order
- Facts: HW-1, HW-2; the image layout above.
- Reasoning: `crt0.S` is the only assembly, and does only what C can't:
  set `sp` and call `sb_start`. `sb_start` (C) copies initialised data from
  the image to RAM, clears zeroed data and the beacon, and calls `main`.
  Clearing matters on the chip even though fwtest starts with RAM at zero
  (HW-7). `main` checks one initialised and one zeroed variable and writes
  the marker only if both are right (otherwise a different marker), so the
  marker proves the runtime as well as the boot. Should `sb_start` ever
  return, `crt0.S` stops on purpose with interrupts off and a jump to
  itself, which fwtest reports as a halt. r0's block pointer (HW-4) is not
  used yet.
- Alternatives: copying data in assembly (rejected: more assembly for no
  gain, as C can run as soon as `sp` is set); no zeroing (rejected: relies
  on fwtest's start state).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the marker and the console
- Facts: HW-26 (a word at a fixed RAM address is visible through `--ram`
  and `--watchdog`), HW-25 (`DBG_MSG` at `0x01EEE244` appends each word
  written to fwtest's console; confirmed by E-2), Q-5 (the SDK marks
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, and whether it does anything on the chip is open).
- Reasoning: the beacon is four words at `0x01C00000`: the marker
  `0x44304253` ("SB0D" in memory order), the beat count, the time base
  value of the last pass, and the period. Tests read it with `--ram`. The
  console line `small-beeps M0d` is a second, human-readable sign that
  `main` ran, written as whole words (HW-25). The SDK's struct declares
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, so it is written through our own pointer at the
  spec's address; on the chip the write may go nowhere (Q-5), and nothing
  depends on it.
- Alternatives: the console only (rejected: Q-5).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: how the heartbeat is timed
- Facts: HW-12 (TIMER4's registers), HW-13 (in fwtest, TIMER4 counts at
  24 MHz once `CON` bit 0 is set; confirmed by E-3), HW-14 (its value when
  stopped and its response to writes: emulator-only), docs/HARNESS.md
  ("Time": a core that waits lets time jump, and captures can come late).
- Reasoning: no interrupts before M1, so `main` polls TIMER4. It sets
  `CON` bit 0, notes `CNT`, and then uses only differences of `CNT`, so it
  relies on nothing in HW-14; unsigned subtraction stays right across a
  32-bit wrap. One beat is 24 000 ticks (1 ms). Each pass counts every
  whole period that has passed (a catch-up loop, not one beat per pass), so
  the count is right however late a pass runs, and stores the time base
  value in the beacon. A beat count that is a pure function of the time
  base can be checked exactly: `beats == ticks / 24000`.
- Experiment (our own, in fwtest through `tools/fwtest`): fwtest treats
  this loop as waiting even though it stores to RAM on every pass: a
  100 ms run took about 36 000 instructions, and captures came 1.2 to
  2.6 ms after the time asked. The heartbeat stays right (above), and the
  stored ticks let the tests check timing regardless: each capture must
  show the right beats for its ticks, taken at most 5 ms late, and at the
  end of a one-second run the ticks must agree with fwtest's emulated time
  within 10 µs (R-BOOT-3, `tools/fw-suite.py`). That end check also
  confirms HW-13's rate on our own.
- Alternatives: a busy loop that keeps core 0 running so captures are
  exact (rejected: it would burn every cycle, and the stored ticks make it
  unnecessary); the tick timer or TIMER5 with interrupts (M1).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: emulator-only facts
- Facts: HW-3, HW-10, HW-14, HW-22 (the emulator-only entries M0d could
  touch).
- Reasoning: M0d relies on none of them. It takes no interrupts (HW-3,
  HW-22), never releases core 1 (HW-10; R-BOOT-4 checks core 1 never ran),
  and uses only differences of TIMER4 (HW-14). Every fact it does rely on
  is confirmed (HW-1, HW-2, HW-4 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26), so
  no extra black-box test of an emulator-only fact is needed; the
  heartbeat's end check (above) re-confirms HW-13 independently.

### 2026-10-22 M0d: build
- Facts: P-1 (the toolchain), P-13 (our compile and link experiments).
- Reasoning: `tools/build.sh` compiles every `.c` and `.S` in
  `firmware/src/` in sorted order and links with `firmware/app.ld`.
  - `-nostdinc`: no C library headers either; `sb.h` defines the few types
    used, and the SDK's register headers are the only outside includes.
  - `-fno-common`: zeroed globals go to `.bss`, where startup clears them,
    not to common symbols.
  - `--no-undefined` and `--orphan-handling=error`: the link fails on any
    missing function (such as a compiler helper we don't provide) and on
    any section the script doesn't place. M0d needs no compiler helpers.
  - Assembly is built without `-g`, which would record the source path.
  - The raw image is the `.text` section then the `.data` section, each
    extracted with `objcopy` and joined: this `objcopy` takes one section
    per run, and `ld --oformat binary` resolved a data address wrongly in
    a trial (`0x01C00000` for a variable at `0x01C00014`). The build checks
    the joined image's length against the layout's.
  - `app.size` (code, data, bss, image, stack) is a build output, so the
    record carries it (C-FW-SIZE). First size: code 252, data 4, bss 20,
    image 256, stack 4096 bytes.
  - Objects are built in the container's `/tmp`, so the outputs are just
    `app.bin`, `app.elf` and `app.size`.
- Alternatives: `ld --oformat binary` (rejected, above).
- `firmware/src/placeholder.c` is removed: nothing uses it any more.
EOF
tail -3 docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md

  depends on it.

### 2026-10-22 M0d: how the heartbeat is timed
- Facts: HW-12 (TIMER4's registers), HW-13 (in fwtest, TIMER4 counts at
  24 MHz once `CON` bit 0 is set; confirmed by E-3), HW-14 (its value when
  stopped and its response to writes: emulator-only), docs/HARNESS.md
  ("Time": a core that waits lets time jump, and captures can come late).

  `CON` bit 0, notes `CNT`, and then uses only differences of `CNT`, so it
  relies on nothing in HW-14; unsigned subtraction stays right across a
  32-bit wrap. One beat is 24 000 ticks (1 ms). Each pass counts every
  whole period that has passed (a catch-up loop, not one beat per pass), so
  the count is right however late a pass runs, and stores the time base
  value in the beacon. A beat count that is a pure function of the time
  base can be checked exactly: `beats == ticks / 24000`.

  this loop as waiting even though it stores to RAM on every pass: a
  100 ms run took about 36 000 instructions, and captures came 1.2 to
  2.6 ms after the time asked. The heartbeat stays right (above), and the
  stored ticks let the tests check timing regardless: each capture must
  show the right beats for its ticks, taken at most 5 ms late, and at the
  end of a one-second run the ticks must agree with fwtest's emulated time
  within 10 µs (R-BOOT-3, `tools/fw-suite.py`). That end check also
  confirms HW-13's rate on our own.

  exact (rejected: it would burn every cycle, and the stored ticks make it
  unnecessary); the tick timer or TIMER5 with interrupts (M1).

  touch).

  HW-22), never releases core 1 (HW-10; R-BOOT-4 checks core 1 never ran),
  and uses only differences of TIMER4 (HW-14). Every fact it does rely on
  is confirmed (HW-1, HW-2, HW-4 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26), so
  no extra black-box test of an emulator-only fact is needed; the
  heartbeat's end check (above) re-confirms HW-13 independently.

    record carries it (C-FW-SIZE). First size: code 252, data 4, bss 20,

content.text: Docs written. Committing in small pieces: firmware + build, then the suite, then the record wiring, then the docs.

input.content:
firmware: startup, linker script and main with a marker and heartbeat

What:    The smallest firmware. firmware/src/crt0.S sets the stack and
         calls sb_start (start.c), which copies initialised data, clears
         zeroed data and runs main (main.c). main checks both, writes the
         marker "SB0D" to a four-word beacon at the start of RAM and a line
         to the debug console, then keeps a heartbeat: one beat per 24 000
         ticks of TIMER4 (1 ms), with the tick count stored beside it.
         firmware/app.ld lays out the image at the code window and RAM up
         to 0x01C7FC00 with a 4 KiB stack at the top. tools/build.sh builds
         every source in firmware/src into app.elf, the raw app.bin and
         app.size (code, data, bss, image, stack). placeholder.c is
         removed: nothing needs it.
Why:     M0d section 2; R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-2, R-BUILD-1, R-REPRO-3.
How:     Written from HARDWARE-SPEC.md, the vendored SDK headers and the
         compiler's own output on test files of ours (the assembly syntax).
         Built with -nostdinc and -fno-common, linked with --no-undefined
         and --orphan-handling=error. The raw image joins the .text and
         .data sections extracted one at a time with objcopy, because this
         objcopy takes one section per run and ld --oformat binary got a
         data address wrong in a trial. No interrupts (M1); the heartbeat
         uses only differences of TIMER4's count. Design choices in
         docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md (a later commit).
Result:  Two builds with the source at different paths: byte-identical.
         Size: code 252, data 4, bss 20, image 256 bytes. In fwtest: the
         marker, the console line and 1000 beats in a 1 s run.
Sources: P-1, P-2, P-13, P-14, P-15
Exposure: firmware side, none

Model: claude-opus-5-5
Claude-Session: b7ed6c1a-fb2a-4707-b9e2-303e11f65740
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

tests: the firmware's fwtest suite and its heartbeat check

What:    tests/fw/boot.suite runs the image in fwtest: "boot" compares the
         marker, the console line and the top of RAM (0x01C7FC00 up) with
         golden files; "heartbeat" runs 1 s under a 5 ms watchdog on the
         beat count and captures the beacon five times.
         tools/fw-suite.py puts the image where the suite expects it, runs

input.new_string:
### M0d: smallest firmware (firmware side)
Startup, linker script and `main` (a marker word, a heartbeat), written only
from `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the SDK and FM-1-RE's documents; booted and checked
with `fwtest`. Design choices explained in docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md.
- Requirements: R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5, R-BUILD-1, R-BUILD-2.
- Done when: CI boots the image in the harness and the record shows the
  marker word and heartbeat.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0d, firmware side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Start**: the clean folder fast-forwarded with lazy fetching off;
    `tools/clean-update.sh` passed. Nothing was left to archive (the
    session the prompt named is this one); `tools/check-transcripts.py`
    PASS.
  - **The firmware** (`firmware/`): `crt0.S` sets the stack and calls
    `sb_start`, which copies initialised data, clears zeroed data and runs
    `main`. `main` writes the marker `SB0D` to a four-word beacon at
    `0x01C00000` and a line to the debug console, then keeps a heartbeat
    of one beat per millisecond of TIMER4, without interrupts. Freestanding
    C11 with `-nostdinc`, no library code of any kind, one assembly file.
    Sources: HW-1 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26 (all confirmed; no
    emulator-only fact relied on), the SDK's `WL82.h`, and our own
    toolchain experiments (PROVENANCE P-13 to P-15).
  - **Size**: code 252, data 4, bss 20 bytes; raw image 256 bytes; stack
    4 KiB reserved. Recorded by C-FW-SIZE (R-BUILD-2).
  - **Tests**: `tests/fw/boot.suite` through `tools/fwtest`, checked by
    `tools/fw-suite.py` (C-FW-SUITE): golden marker, console line and top
    of RAM; a one-second heartbeat whose time base agrees with fwtest's
    emulated time within 10 µs. Requirements R-BOOT-3 to R-BOOT-5 and
    R-BUILD-2 added.
  - **Found on the way**: fwtest counts the heartbeat's polling loop as
    waiting even though it stores to RAM each pass, so captures came up to
    1.6 ms late; the beacon's stored tick count keeps the timing checks
    exact (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md). `ld --oformat binary` resolved a data
    address wrongly, so the raw image is made with `objcopy`.
  - `firmware/src/placeholder.c` removed. M0e is next.

-### 2026-10-22 M0d: memory layout
-- Facts: HW-1 (the image runs from its first byte at `0x02000000`), HW-5

-  1 MiB less 16 KiB), HW-6 (main RAM is 512 KiB from `0x01C00000` on the

-  HW-4 (the block r0 points to at `0x01C7FC00` in fwtest), HW-7 (fwtest has
-  1 MiB of main RAM and two more banks, not known on the chip, Q-1),
-  HW-18 (the vector table at `0x01C7FE00`). `firmware/app.ld`.
-- Reasoning: code and constants run in place from the image (the window
-  is readable and executable), so only data that changes takes RAM. RAM is
-  limited to what the chip has and stops at `0x01C7FC00`: that keeps the
-  r0 block (wanted later for booting on the chip, Q-11), the SDK's reserved
-  area and the vector table out of reach of anything this image does,
-  which R-BOOT-5's golden capture checks. Order in RAM: the beacon first,
-  at a fixed address the tests name; then zeroed data; then initialised
-  data, whose bytes the image carries right after the code; the stack at
-  the top. The beacon and `.bss` are one contiguous range, so startup
-  clears both with one loop. The linker script asserts the fixed
-  addresses and that data never reaches the stack.
-- Alternatives: using fwtest's larger RAM (rejected: an image that only
-  fits fwtest proves less); putting the beacon in `.data` (rejected: its
-  address would move whenever data is added).
-- Facts: HW-2 (every register but r0 is 0 at entry, both stack pointers
-  included: no stack until the image sets one), HW-3 (core 0 starts in user
-  mode; interrupts would switch to `ssp`, emulator-only), the compiler's
-  data layout for pi32v2 (no type is aligned to more than 4 bytes; P-13).
-- Reasoning: the first instruction sets `sp` to `0x01C7FC00`, before any C
-  runs; 4 KiB is reserved below it. M0d's C uses a few words at most (the
-  compiler keeps `sb_start` and `main` in registers), so 4 KiB is ample
-  and cheap. The top is 8-byte aligned, more than the data layout needs,
-  so nothing changes if 8-byte types arrive. Only the user-mode `sp` is
-  set: M0d takes no interrupts, so `ssp` is left for M1, which must set it
-  before enabling them (HW-3).
-- Alternatives: a stack at the very top of RAM (rejected: it would run
-  through the reserved area and the vector table).
-### 2026-10-22 M0d: startup order
-- Facts: HW-1, HW-2; the image layout above.
-- Reasoning: `crt0.S` is the only assembly, and does only what C can't:
-  set `sp` and call `sb_start`. `sb_start` (C) copies initialised data from
-  the image to RAM, clears zeroed data and the beacon, and calls `main`.
-  Clearing matters on the chip even though fwtest starts with RAM at zero
-  (HW-7). `main` checks one initialised and one zeroed variable and writes
-  the marker only if both are right (otherwise a different marker), so the
-  marker proves the runtime as well as the boot. Should `sb_start` ever
-  return, `crt0.S` stops on purpose with interrupts off and a jump to
-  itself, which fwtest reports as a halt. r0's block pointer (HW-4) is not
-  used yet.

-  gain, as C can run as soon as `sp` is set); no zeroing (rejected: relies
-  on fwtest's start state).
-### 2026-10-22 M0d: the marker and the console
-- Facts: HW-26 (a word at a fixed RAM address is visible through `--ram`
-  and `--watchdog`), HW-25 (`DBG_MSG` at `0x01EEE244` appends each word
-  written to fwtest's console; confirmed by E-2), Q-5 (the SDK marks

-  value of the last pass, and the period. Tests read it with `--ram`. The
-  console line `small-beeps M0d` is a second, human-readable sign that

-  `DBG_MSG` read-only, so it is written through our own pointer at the

+  limited to what the chip has and stops at `0x01C7FC00`: that keeps the
+  r0 block (wanted later for booting on the chip, Q-11), the SDK's reserved

import sys

RULES = [
    ("private key", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----.*?-----END[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"),
     "[REDACTED:private-key]"),
    ("GitHub token", re.compile(r"\b(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,})"),
     "[REDACTED:github-token]"),
    ("Anthropic key", re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}"), "[REDACTED:anthropic-key]"),
    ("AWS key ID", re.compile(r"\b(AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"), "[REDACTED:aws-key]"),
    ("bearer token", re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]{20,}=*"), "Bearer [REDACTED]"),
    ("account or organisation ID",
     re.compile(r'("(?:owner)?(?:[Aa]ccount|[Oo]rganization)(?:Uuid|Id|UUID|_uuid|_id)"\s*:\s*")[^"]+(")'),
     r"\1[REDACTED:account-id]\2"),
    ("e-mail address",
     re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"),
     "[REDACTED:email]"),
    ("home folder path", re.compile(r"/(?:Users|home)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?=/|\b)"), "~"),
    ("per-user temp path", re.compile(r"/private/tmp/claude-\d+/|/tmp/claude-\d+/"), "/tmp/claude-UID/"),
    ("project folder name", re.compile(r"-Users-[A-Za-z0-9._]+-"), "-HOME-"),
]
# no-reply addresses are kept: they identify authors without being private
KEEP_EMAIL = re.compile(r"noreply@|@users\.noreply\.github\.com")


HOST_RULE = ("host name", re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9-]+\.local\b(?!\.)"), "[REDACTED:host]")
HOME_USER = re.compile(r"/(?:Users|home)/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/")


def user_rules(path):
    """Rules for the local user names seen in home-folder paths, so they are
    also redacted where they appear alone (e.g. in `ls -l` output)."""
    names = set()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            names.update(HOME_USER.findall(line))
    names -= {"Shared", "runner"}
    return [("local user name", re.compile(r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(n)), "[REDACTED:user]")
            for n in sorted(names)]


SPEC_DIRS = ("vendor/emulator/", "harness/", "sessions/spec/")
# One line of a git summary inside a JSON string: " path | 12 +-" or

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,

    ap.add_argument("transcript")
    ap.add_argument("--role", required=True, choices=("clean", "spec"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None,

    ap.add_argument("--archived-by", default="",
                    help="the session doing the archiving, for the note")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.out is None:

    src = a.transcript
    sid = os.path.basename(src)[:-len(".jsonl")]
    name = "%s-%s-%s" % (first_date(src), a.role, sid)
    dst = os.path.join(a.out, name + ".jsonl")
    if os.path.exists(dst):
        raise SystemExit("refusing to overwrite %s" % dst)
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)

    counts = {}
    files = [(src, dst)]
    subs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(src), sid, "subagents", "*.jsonl")))
    if subs:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(a.out, name + ".subagents"))
        files += [(s, os.path.join(a.out, name + ".subagents", os.path.basename(s))) for s in subs]
    extra = []
    for s, _ in files:
        extra += [r for r in user_rules(s) if r[1].pattern not in [e[1].pattern for e in extra]]
    spec_files = spec_names() if a.role == "clean" else None
    hashes = []
    for s, d in files:
        hs, hd = redact_file(s, d, counts, extra, spec_files)
        hashes.append((os.path.relpath(d, a.out), hs, hd))

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Archives a finished session's transcript into sessions/ (R-CLEAN-3).

  archive-session.py TRANSCRIPT.jsonl --role clean|spec [--out sessions/<role>]

Run it at the start of the next session (never on the live session). A
clean session archives only clean sessions; a spec session may archive
either (sessions/README.md). It copies the transcript to
`sessions/<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` (the date is
the UTC date of its first entry), along with any subagent transcripts
(`<id>/subagents/*.jsonl` next to it) into `<same name>.subagents/`. It
redacts:
  - tokens and keys (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, bearer tokens, private keys);
  - e-mail addresses, except no-reply addresses;
  - account and organisation IDs;
  - private paths: home folders become `~`, and per-user temp folders are
    shortened;
  - the local user names seen in those paths, wherever they appear, and
    `*.local` host names;
  - in clean transcripts only: the lines of a git summary (a merge's
    diffstat, `create mode` and `delete mode` lines) that name files under
    vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/. Each run of such lines
    becomes one note saying how many were removed. A name shortened to
    `.../tail` counts when its tail matches only such files.
It writes `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside the copy, saying what was
redacted and how many times, with the SHA-256 of the original and of the
copy. Every redacted line must still parse as JSON. It refuses to overwrite
an existing archive.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
def redact_line(line, counts, extra=(), spec_files=None):
    for name, rx, repl in list(RULES) + [HOST_RULE] + list(extra):
        if name == "e-mail address":
            def sub(m):
                if KEEP_EMAIL.search(m.group(0)):
                    return m.group(0)
                counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
                return repl
            line = rx.sub(sub, line)
            continue
        line, n = rx.subn(repl, line)
        if n:
            counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + n
    if spec_files is not None:
        line = redact_spec_paths(line, counts, spec_files)
    return line


def redact_file(src, dst, counts, extra=(), spec_files=None):
    h_src, h_dst = hashlib.sha256(), hashlib.sha256()
    with open(src, "rb") as f, open(dst, "wb") as out:
        for n, raw in enumerate(f, 1):
            h_src.update(raw)
            line = redact_line(raw.decode("utf-8"), counts, extra, spec_files)
            if line.strip():
                try:
                    json.loads(line)
                except ValueError as e:
                    raise SystemExit("%s:%d: redaction broke the JSON (%s)" % (src, n, e))
            data = line.encode("utf-8")
            h_dst.update(data)
            out.write(data)

    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    # REUSE-IgnoreStart
    note = ["<!--", "SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT",
            "SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", "-->", "",
            # REUSE-IgnoreEnd
            "# Redactions: %s" % name, "",
            "- Session: `%s` (%s side)" % (sid, a.role),
            "- Archived: %s%s" % (now, (" by " + a.archived_by) if a.archived_by else ""),
            "- Tool: tools/archive-session.py (its RULES list is the full redaction policy)",
            "", "## What was redacted", ""]
    if counts:
        note += ["| Kind | Count |", "|------|-------|"]
        note += ["| %s | %d |" % (k, counts[k]) for k in sorted(counts)]
    else:
        note.append("Nothing.")
    note += ["", "Nothing else was changed. Redactions replace text in place, so every line",
             "is still the same JSON entry.", "",
             "## Files", "",
             "| File | SHA-256 of the original | SHA-256 of this copy |",
             "|------|-------------------------|----------------------|"]
    note += ["| `%s` | `%s` | `%s` |" % h for h in hashes]
    note.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(a.out, name + ".REDACTIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(note))
    print("archived %s -> %s" % (src, dst))
    for k in sorted(counts):
        print("  redacted %-28s %d" % (k, counts[k]))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from tests.helpers import load_tool

cp = load_tool("check-private.py")


class PrivateTermsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-PUB-3"""

    def test_hit_lines_ignore_case_and_count_lines(self):
        data = b"one\nTwo SECRET\nthree\nsecret and secret\n"
        self.assertEqual(cp.hit_lines(data, [b"secret"]), [2, 4])
        self.assertEqual(cp.hit_lines(data, [b"absent"]), [])

    def test_reports_file_and_line_only(self):
        files = {"a.md": b"fine\nhas Secret\n", "b.md": b"fine\n"}
        problems = cp.check_files(sorted(files), files.get, [b"secret"], {},
                                  lambda p, d: "blob-" + p)
        self.assertEqual(problems, ["a.md:2"])
        self.assertFalse(any("ecret" in p for p in problems))

    def test_allowed_only_at_the_exact_blob(self):
        files = {"a.md": b"has secret\n"}
        blob = lambda p, d: "h1" if d == b"has secret\n" else "h2"
        self.assertEqual(cp.check_files(["a.md"], files.get, [b"secret"], {"a.md": "h1"}, blob), [])
        files["a.md"] = b"has secret\nand more\n"
        self.assertEqual(cp.check_files(["a.md"], files.get, [b"secret"], {"a.md": "h1"}, blob),
                         ["a.md:1"])

    def test_files_not_on_disk_are_skipped(self):
        self.assertEqual(cp.check_files(["gone"], lambda p: None, [b"x"], {}, None), [])

    def test_terms_from_environment(self):
        saved = os.environ.get("PRIVATE_TERMS")
        os.environ["PRIVATE_TERMS"] = "# comment\n  Alpha \n\nbeta\nalpha\n"
        try:
            self.assertEqual(cp.load_terms(), [b"alpha", b"beta"])
        finally:
            if saved is None:
                del os.environ["PRIVATE_TERMS"]
            else:
                os.environ["PRIVATE_TERMS"] = saved

    def test_blob_hash_matches_git(self):
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("wb", delete=False) as f:
            f.write(b"hello\n")
        try:
            self.assertEqual(cp.blob_hash(None, b"hello\n"),
                             "ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a")
        finally:
            os.unlink(f.name)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            else:

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for [REDACTED:user] — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you [REDACTED:user]'s pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Session-specific guidance
 - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.
 - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.
 - If the user asks about "ultrareview" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `~/.claude/projects/-HOME-Development-[REDACTED:private]-clean/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown

name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>

  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead.
